newsitem.title: FRANCE: Experts exclude radar fault in Airbus crash.
newsitem.headline: Experts exclude radar fault in Airbus crash.

text.p: An expert report has ruled out failure of the onboard positioning system in an Airbus plane which crashed in 1992, killing 87 people, a group representing the victims' families said on Wednesday.
Two specialists, Pierre Nouvel and Patrick Anglade, concluded that a radar malfunction did not cause the crash, the group said.

Investigating magistrate Francois Guichard asked Nouvel, an antenna specialist, and Anglade, a telemetry expert, on July 13 to look into the positioning system after doubts were raised over its reliability.
Airbus Industrie , which builds the A320, declined comment.
"This is an attempt to whitewash Airbus," Alvaro Rendon, chairman of the families' group, said after receiving a copy of the expert report.
The group claims an excess of metal in the protective skin covering the antenna used for the visual, omni-range-distance (VOR-DME) positioning system, misled the pilot.
Metal strips are used to conduct lightning in the protective skin, which is composed mainly of non-conducting composites.
Guichard commissioned the latest report after another technical expert, Max Venet, changed his mind and said the positioning system may have given erroneous information and contributed to the crash.
The onboard VOR-DME system tracks a radio signal sent from a transmitter at the base of a runway and allows the crew to locate themselves in relation to the airport.
The A320 of the ex-Air Inter domestic airline flew into Mont Saint-Odile on January 20, 1992, as it attempted an approach on Strasbourg airport.

The magistrate has placed under investigation three executives of Air Inter, recently renamed Air France Europe, two officials of the DGAC civil aviation authority, and the man in charge of air traffic control at Strasbourg at the time.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
